title: Copepod Swimming Biomechanics of Labidocera aestiva
content: The use of animal models remains a mainstay in the understanding, development, and advancement of human and clinical research, and is often a crucial component in the implementation of prosthetic and biomechanical devices. Our research investigates the unique swimming mechanism of a rather infinitesimal organism, but one that may have an immense impact on our understanding of joint biomechanics and prosthetic design. To recognize the potential contribution of copepods to this field, this paper thoroughly examines the anatomy and articulations of Labidocera aestiva, specifically its pleopods, and determines how these structures contribute to its unique swimming stroke.
